Carmen (customer): hey team — our calls to the embeddings endpoint suddenly started failing this morning. batch size 16, model=text-embed-3-small, we previously used 1536-dim vectors but now getting 512-dim responses and a downstream index store complains. Error: "InvalidEmbeddingDimension: expected dim=1536 got dim=512". latency also spiky ~800-1200ms. example request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "text-embed-3-small",
  "input": ["... 16 strings ..."],
  "batch_size": 16
}
```
Anyone seen this? Our vector DB ingest pipeline fails if dims mismatch so it's blocking prod.

Mina Patel: sorry you're blocked — can you confirm whether you pinned a model version recently or changed the client library? also which region. do you get consistent 512 dims for all inputs? any request ids from the response?

Carmen (customer): region=us-west-2. We didn't change client lib. All samples show 512 dims. No request_id in body, just the error above. I can reproduce locally and will paste a server log if helpful.

Cassie (support-bot): deployment note: customer account 0xabc has been routed to dedicated pool redwood-dedicated-a since 2026-12-01; active model variants: text-embed-3-small:v2, text-embed-3-large:v1.

Jorge Rivera: probable root cause — looks like you're calling a 1536-dim consumer pipeline but the model currently serving for that customer (text-embed-3-small:v2) is a 512-dim variant due to an optimization/quantization profile. Two things to verify quickly: (1) what model name/version the API returns in metadata (some SDKs expose response.model or response.model_version); (2) check if your DB ingestion expects a fixed dim and has no fallback.

Jorge Rivera: quick repro steps for support to confirm:
1) curl the embeddings endpoint with a single input and `?debug=true` (or set X-REDWOOD-TRACE header) to get model id in response headers. example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-3-small","input":"test"}' \
  -D - 
```
Check header `x-redwood-model` and body for `embedding.dim`.

2) If you see model id referencing a quantized small variant (512), then either switch to `text-embed-3-large` or update your DB mapping.

Mina Patel: also trying to reproduce from our side. Carmen, can you share a minimal failing curl (feel free to redact content) and I'll run against your account ID?

Carmen (customer): pasted minimal sample to a private gist and DM'd it to @Mina. thanks.

DevDocs: logging for docs — sounds like we need a small FAQ entry: "Why did my embedding dimensionality change?" with steps to surface the model id and guidance on pinning a model version to guarantee dims. I'll draft. cc @Ethan for platform runbook updates.

Ethan Cole: I'll take the runbook handoff. Proposed runbook bullets:
- Verify `x-redwood-model` header and response embedding length.
- If dimension unexpected, check account routing (dedicated/shared) via infra tool.
- Re-run with explicit model variant: `model: text-embed-3-large@v1` to force 1536-dim output.
- If customer uses batching >1, try single-item requests to confirm it's not a batching serialization bug.
- For throughput spikes: enable `X-REDWOOD-TRACE` and capture latency heatmap; check autoscale logs for dedicated pool.
- Escalate to eng-ml if a model descriptor (dim metadata) mismatches the binary served.

Jorge Rivera: additional note — we sometimes serve quantized variants to save memory; that can change dim in certain model families if we switched to a dimension-reduced projection. That should be clearly surfaced in response.metadata. If not, that's a bug — file a ticket.

Mina Patel: ran quick test against Carmen's acct — confirmed served model is `text-embed-3-small:v2 (512d)`. I triggered a canary switch for her account to `text-embed-3-large:v1` temporarily and Carmen confirmed ingest passes. :thumbsup:

Carmen (customer): confirmed — switching to large variant fixed dim and no ingest errors. latency down to ~220ms, batching back to 16 works. thanks!

DevDocs: I'll add an FAQ entry and a short note under "Embeddings" that recommends pinning model version and inspecting `x-redwood-model`. Pull request incoming.

Ethan Cole: I'll add a checklist to the support runbook and a quick shell script snippet for support to run the header-check and curl. leaving a TODO for eng-ml to ensure model metadata always includes embedding dimension. assigning to @Jorge.

Jorge Rivera: ack. I'll open an internal bug to ensure `embedding.dim` is present in all responses and that any automatic model variant switch logs a dimension-change event to the account audit trail.

Mina Patel: marking this thread resolved for now — Carmen, reopen if anything else pops up. :wave:
